# sitegen

Static site generator for a small blog. Builds `content/` Markdown into `out/` HTML.

## Layout

- `content/posts/*.md` -- blog posts (front-matter: title, date)
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` -- top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` -- shared template with `{{title}}`, `{{nav}}`, `{{stylesheet}}`, `{{content}}` placeholders
- `static/style.css` -- shared stylesheet
- `build.py` -- build script (stdlib only)
- `tests/test_build.py` -- unit tests

## Build & test

    python3 build.py
    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

## Key behavior

- Posts go to `out/posts/<slug>.html`; top-level pages to `out/<slug>.html`
- Nav and stylesheet links use relative prefixes (posts use `../`)
- Index lists all posts sorted by date (newest first)
- Markdown subset: headings (#, ##, ###), paragraphs, links, **bold**

Done. The site builds clean, all 6 tests pass, and every link resolves.

**What was wrong:** Post pages (`out/posts/*.html`) had broken nav links and stylesheet paths — they pointed to `index.html` and `style.css` instead of `../index.html` and `../style.css`. Clicking "Home" from a post would 404 because `posts/index.html` doesn't exist.

**What I changed:**
- `build.py` — `nav_html()` and `render_page()` now take a `prefix` parameter. Post pages pass `prefix="../"`, top-level pages use `""`.
- `templates/page.html` — replaced the hardcoded `style.css` with `{{stylesheet}}` so the template fills in the right path.
- `tests/test_build.py` — added `test_all_links_resolve`, which parses every built HTML file and asserts each `<a href>` and `<link href>` resolves to a real file. This is a regression guard so the handoff can't silently re-break.

The rest (build script, front-matter parsing, markdown subset, index listing) was already working. Your colleague can add posts by dropping a `.md` file in `content/posts/` and running `python3 build.py`.
